C-SCHEMA-REFERENCE.Summary: Deliver RM-GOVERNED-PATH P1 step 4 only: generate a committed schema reference from the declarative inventories in src/artifact/grammar.ts, fail CI when that file is stale, and extend lint explain to those same inventories as named shapes, so the markdown and the explain surface have one source. Glob matching semantics are out: F60 blocks P1.4's requirement to document zero-depth globstar, and deleting the duplicate matcher is P2.1, not this bundle.
C-SCHEMA-REFERENCE.Problem:
**Shared shape.** P1.4 exists so an agent can author a valid artifact without reading TypeScript. A hand-written schema document becomes a second grammar and drifts. The step therefore asks for generation from the grammar, a committed file, a CI stale-check, and explain of shapes from the same source. Authoring HEAD a26b07b, packaged 6.2.0, lint 0/0 across 127 artifacts, active changes empty, suite 1286 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail. Those numbers are a snapshot (F33).
---
**The grammar is not a declarative schema.** src/artifact/grammar.ts is 2387 lines of imperative validators. It has a declarative core: eighteen module-private constants (section lists, scope tags, anchor families, root tags, statuses, verdict outcomes, gate values, clarification form, design-reference children). They are const, not export const. The generator can honestly document those inventories and nothing else. Presenting the result as a complete schema is F10. C-EXPLAIN-COVERAGE already recorded that P1.4 would open this file; that is not a licence to claim the imperative remainder.
---
**Explain today takes an issue code.** The lint explain argument is one string. classifyIssueCode and formatLintExplanation treat it as a code. Extending the same argument to shapes needs a disambiguation rule. Across the registered union (exact guides, review catalog, gate catalog, collectEmittedIssueCodes, PREFIX_GUIDES prefixes) every member contains a period. Four GraceCommandError codes (invalid-arguments, invalid-project, ambiguous-target, not-found) do not, and already classify as unknown. A period-only rule therefore holds for the lint/review/gate universe and fails the moment a shape name contains a period or a new code does not. That is an F10 waiting to happen.
The step's own examples (graph-module, module-contract) are not among the eighteen inventories. module-contract is a marker family in project-utils.ts. Graph module Type values live in types.ts MODULE_TYPES and are checked in projections.ts. Registering those names here would make the generator claim a source it does not read.
---
**F60 blocks the step's globstar sentence.** P1.4 says the reference must document zero-depth globstar explicitly (see P2.1). Sequencing rule 4 orders P1.4 before P2.1's release note on that premise. Re-measured at this HEAD, the product implements glob matching twice and the copies disagree:
web/js/**/*.js x web/js/app.js review false scope true src/**/*.ts x src/a.ts review false scope true src/**/*.ts x src/x/a.ts review true scope true src/** x src/a.ts review true scope true
src/artifact/scope.ts (parseScopeGlob / observedWriteScopeContains) is segment-based, exported, and already admits zero-depth globstar. src/review/core.ts matchSimpleGlob is a private regex copy that requires at least one intervening segment. The copy governs the scope audit. A plan declaring Glob src/**/*.ts and writing src/a.ts is inside approved ObservedWriteScope by the canonical parser and reported outside it by the audit.
A generated reference cannot be the single truth about a rule implemented two ways. Deleting the duplicate is P2.1 (D11: genuine conflict, not filing). This bundle must not document zero-depth globstar, and must not quietly omit the refusal: the generated preamble names glob matching as outside coverage and states why.
---
**docs/schema-reference.md does not exist.** docs/ currently holds ngrace-explainer.html and plans/. Markdown under docs/ is not an XML artifact and is not scanned as governed markup. ignoredDirs lists examples and scripts, so a writer under scripts/ is outside ngrace lint. Without a stale-check that can be shown red, a committed generated file is just a document (F28 / F35.1).

Goals.Goal: **Generated reference.** A committed docs/schema-reference.md is produced from the live declarative inventories in grammar.ts, not hand-written. Regeneration on a clean tree is a no-op. The file's preamble names every shape it covers and names the classes it does not.

**Detectable staleness.** Changing an inventory member without regenerating fails a check that validate:ci runs. Absence of the committed file also fails that check. Green on a clean tree is the baseline, not the evidence.

**Explain shapes from the same renderer.** lint explain accepts each registered shape name and prints that shape's section as the renderer produced it for the markdown. Issue-code explain is unchanged. Disambiguation is registry-first, decided below.
**F60 recorded, not improvised.** The generated document does not teach a glob matching rule. It discloses that P1.4 asked for zero-depth globstar and that F60 blocks it.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REFERENCE-GENERATED: docs/schema-reference.md exists in the repository and is byte-identical to the renderer output for the full registry. A generated banner is the first line and tells a reader not to hand-edit. Each GRAMMAR_INVENTORIES property is the same reference as the validator constant of the same name. Each inventory member appears in the generated text as that live value, so a hardcoded copy inside the renderer fails when the constant moves. The writer script is what updates the committed file. **HEAD today:** the path does not exist; the barrel does not exist; the renderer does not exist. **Failure conditions:** a hand-written file sold as generated; renderer copies member lists instead of reading the barrel; barrel rebuilds arrays or Sets so reference equality fails; banner absent; only a subset of registered shapes rendered while claiming the registry; writer not the update path.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-COVERAGE-NAMED: The generated file's preamble, before any shape section, names every registered shape and states that coverage is those inventories only. It names three excluded classes as excluded: imperative validators in grammar.ts; file-local markup families (and that graph-module and module-contract are in that class, not in this registry); glob matching (F60). It does not describe itself as a complete schema or a complete grammar. **HEAD today:** no file, so no preamble. **Failure conditions:** preamble omitted; file titled or introduced as a complete schema; excluded class missing; graph-module or module-contract presented as covered; a count of inventories or shapes frozen as the pass bar (F33).
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-DRIFT-DETECTABLE: Two facts, both required. (1) The writer's check mode exits non-zero when docs/schema-reference.md is missing or when its bytes differ from the renderer. validate:ci invokes that check mode. (2) The suite asserts byte-identity and live interpolation as in AC-REFERENCE-GENERATED, so an inventory edit without regeneration fails bun test as well. At pre-change HEAD (1) fails because the file is absent; that absence is this criterion's red, not silence after the file lands. Regeneration on a clean post-change tree is a no-op (zero diff). **HEAD today:** file absent; no check mode; validate:ci does not invoke one. **Failure conditions:** check implemented only as a test that can be skipped; check compares a fixture copy rather than the renderer; green-on-clean-tree sold as the red; HEAD absence not recorded as the red; validate:ci composition unchanged so CI can pass with a stale file if the test is skipped.
